chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) heard a woman when Uthman ibn Maz'un died, and she was saying, 'Congratulations to you, O Abu Al-Saib, [for] Paradise!' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And what is your knowledge? It suffices you to say,

So when Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), passed away, the eye of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed with tears. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we do not say that which angers the Lord, and indeed we are grieving for you, O Ibrahim.'

Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saw a flaw in his grave, so he smoothed it with his hand. Then he said, 'When one of you does a deed, let him perfect it.' Then he said, 'Go with your righteous predecessor, Uthman ibn Maz'un.'

key_terms.عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ: Uthman ibn Maz'un, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.لَا نَقُولُ مَا يُسْخِطُ الرَّبَّ: We do not say that which angers the Lord

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet weeping for his son Ibrahim and how does it relate to Uthman ibn Maz'un?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia understanding of *al-fitra* (natural disposition) by contrasting the Prophet’s measured grief for his son Ibrahim with the woman’s excessive praise of Uthman ibn Maz'un. It establishes that weeping and heartache are permissible signs of humanity, provided they do not lead to saying what displeases Allah, while also emphasizing the importance of *itqan* (excellence/detail) in one's deeds, as seen in the Prophet smoothing the grave. This narrative reinforces the balance between emotional authenticity and theological precision in Shia tradition.
